text:
Charlie McAvoy is driving play like a No. 1 defenseman and getting very little to show for it. Boston takes 62% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, almost 12 points better than without him. Yet his team has scored 4.5 fewer goals than those chances deserved while he's out there, and he has one goal of his own.

That's the story of his last ten: four assists, three of them in one game (the 7-5 win over Washington), and a Bruins team that has lost four of its last six. He's playing heavy minutes through it, nearly 27 on Friday against Toronto.

Evolving-Hockey's read from last season matches what we see: real play-driving value (88th percentile among defensemen) against top competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he's a genuine setup man from the back end. Our talent range puts his scoring rate well above where it sits now. When the finishing around him turns, his points should follow, and we'd expect Boston's results to come with them.
